cross_run_source: run_20260904T140437Z/artifacts/eda/iteration_001_eda_daily_data.csv (pre-parsed daily CSV; same 3212 XMLs, same dedup/filter protocol, 2897 trading-day rows — re-parsing skipped)

salesdata.protocol_notes: dual XML schema (pre-migration: order/orderdetail, post-migration: sale/saledetail); POS filter referencepointofsales=001; argcod=1 for bread; dedup by latest export_timestamp per salesdate (95 duplicate dates)

productdata.note: 278 = count of rows with argcod=1 in productdata.csv catalog; prior runs report 139 unique bread articles SOLD in branch 01 — discrepancy not yet reconciled; see methodological_cautions

storedata.key_finding: confirms regime change 2020-06-01 (shop went 7/7; Mondays closed before this date)

weatherdata.note: hourly data; daily aggregation required before feature engineering; Location and Heat_Index columns can be dropped

VerlofConcurrent_2.csv.reason: exact duplicate of VC1 with one additional StoreKey column; zero unique signal

deliverydata.reason: wholesale delivery channel; no branch 01 retail sales tie-in confirmed; consistent with prior runs

trend.interpretation: trend-stationary (not a random walk); persistent downward trend over 10-year period

regime_change.change_type: structural — day-of-week pattern AND level both change; Mondays added as trading days post-2020-06-01
regime_change.caution: 2020 post-regime period also overlaps with COVID-19 lockdown (Belgium lockdown from 2020-03-18); 24 zero-demand days in 2020 likely COVID closures; the -10.5% level drop may be partly COVID, not purely regime effect

2014_sparse.likely_cause: data export gap or system event; confirmed in protocol.json

feasibility.reasoning: daily bread quantity is count-like positive integer; absolute error aligns with operational planning; MAPE unsafe given 50 zero-demand days; RMSE would penalise rare extreme days disproportionately
feasibility.ts_suitability: strong weekly seasonality (ACF lag-6=0.582 dominant); medium-horizon autocorrelation significant (lag-30=0.500, lag-60=0.465, lag-90=0.418); ADF confirms stationarity — ARIMA-family suitable alongside tree-based; rolling-origin CV required due to regime change
domain_research_flags: Belgian public holidays: expected to explain zero-demand days (50 total); must be verified against calendar
Gentse Feesten (Ghent festival, ~10 days mid-July): spike or dip possible; annual event in training window
COVID-19: Belgium lockdown 2020-03-18; explains 24 zero-demand days in 2020; training model must not generalise lockdown pattern as normal
2014 sparse data: 64 trading days vs ~250 expected; cause unknown; may need to exclude 2014 from rolling-origin folds or flag as anomaly year

provisional_baselines.method: same-DOW seasonal naive with horizon-specific lookback (k = 6 trading-days before regime change, 7 after)
provisional_baselines.note: PROVISIONAL ONLY — these are rough upper-bound baselines computed on full training series; authoritative baseline_floor comes from the baseline skill which scores all 6 fixed rules on the held-out validation rows

join_plan.sales_grain: one row per trading day per branch; non-trading days absent from series
join_plan.weather_join: aggregate hourly Date_time rows to calendar date (daily aggregates: mean temp, max temp, min temp, total precipitation, etc.); left join on date; NaN for pre-2015 dates (feature engineering handles with imputation or lag truncation)
join_plan.competitor_join: left join VerlofConcurrent.csv on date; 0/null for pre-2017 dates
join_plan.target_by_horizon: DATE JOIN only — for horizon h, target = bread_quantity on (row.date + h); never positional shift; guarantees correct alignment across trading-day calendar

agent_initiated_findings.finding: Bread articles catalog count discrepancy: 278 from productdata.csv argcod=1 filter vs 139 unique bread articles reported sold in branch 01 by prior runs. Likely explanation: productdata.csv catalogs all chain articles; 139 = articles with at least one sale in branch 01. Does not affect compiled daily CSV (already branch-01-filtered), but Preprocess should verify and document the exact set of article codes used.
agent_initiated_findings.action_taken: flagged as methodological caution; noted in do_not_repeat that using catalog count (278) as ground truth would be incorrect

agent_initiated_findings.finding: Weather parquet temporal column is 'Date_time' (not 'date', 'timestamp', or 'Date'). The EDA coverage detection code initially tested the wrong column (Location, 100% null) giving NaT. Corrected by explicitly specifying Date_time. Any downstream code must use 'Date_time' not a generic name.

ACF lag-1 = 0.325 is lower than expected for a daily retail series (prior sonnet run reported ~0.73). The difference is likely due to within-week DOW variance dominating the lag-1 autocorrelation; the 50 zero-demand days may also suppress short-lag correlation. The dominant seasonality is weekly (lag-6=0.582 pre-regime), not daily carry-forward.
agent_initiated_findings.action_taken: noted; does not change modeling approach

agent_initiated_findings.finding: 2020 zero-demand days (24 of 50 total) cluster in the COVID lockdown period (March-May 2020). The post-regime period begins 2020-06-01, so the 2020 post-regime rows (n=214) are relatively COVID-free (shop reopened). However, the 6-month pre-regime period of 2020 contains 24 zero-demand days. Rolling-origin CV folds must be constructed carefully so that COVID zero-demand days in train do not bias short-horizon naive predictor features.

handoff.read_this_first: Dominant seasonality is weekly (ACF lag-6=0.582 pre-regime, 7-day period post-regime); 50 zero-demand days exist (24 in 2020 COVID lockdown, rest likely public holidays); the 2020 pre-regime period is anomalous — these zero-demand days MUST be treated with domain knowledge from the domain_research step before any naive predictor features are built.

trading_day_rule.value: exclude Monday when date < 2020-06-01; include all 7 days (Mon-Sun) from 2020-06-01 onward
trading_day_rule.why: storedata Winkelfile.csv confirms shop was closed Mondays before regime change; including pre-regime Mondays would add spurious zeros

dedup_rule.value: keep row with latest export_timestamp per salesdate; 95 duplicate dates exist in raw XML
dedup_rule.why: re-exports contain corrections; earlier export for same date is superseded

zero_demand_handling.value: include zero-demand days in the target series; add binary flag is_zero_demand; do NOT drop from the series
zero_demand_handling.why: zero-demand days are real (closures/holidays) and affect multi-day ahead forecasts; dropping would create gaps that break date-join target construction

regime_change_date.why: storedata-confirmed structural break; seasonal period changes from 6 to 7 trading days/week; rolling-origin CV must span this boundary

pre_parsed_csv_path.why: pre-parsed from 3212 XMLs with identical protocol; 2897 trading-day rows; re-parsing unnecessary

target_column.why: user-specified target; daily sum of units sold for argcod=1 articles at branch 01

recommended_metric.why: MAPE unsafe (50 zero-demand days); MAE aligns with operational planning; consistent with provisional baselines already in MAE units

forecast_horizons.why: user-specified; one champion model per horizon

weather_temporal_column.why: parquet uses 'Date_time' not 'date' or 'timestamp'; other column names give NaT on coverage detection

durable_rules.rule: Per-horizon targets must be created by DATE JOIN (row.date + h calendar days), never by positional shift
durable_rules.why: trading-day calendar has gaps (non-trading days absent); positional shift row[i+h] would align to a different calendar date than expected when gaps fall in the lookahead window
durable_rules.cost_if_broken: model trains on wrong future date's demand; validation metrics will look plausible but reflect misaligned targets — silent corruption

durable_rules.rule: Seasonal period is 6 trading days per week before 2020-06-01 and 7 trading days per week from 2020-06-01
durable_rules.why: Monday closed pre-regime; lag and rolling window features must use k=6 pre-regime and k=7 post-regime for same-DOW lookbacks
durable_rules.cost_if_broken: same-DOW lag features cross DOW boundaries; a 'lag-7' pre-regime picks up a different DOW than intended

durable_rules.rule: Rolling-origin CV folds must include and straddle the 2020-06-01 regime change boundary
durable_rules.why: regime change is structural; CV restricted to pre-regime only would not test generalisation to post-regime period; planner.md requires rolling-origin CV where regime change exists
durable_rules.cost_if_broken: validation metrics are optimistic for post-regime; champion may not generalise to the forecast window

durable_rules.rule: Weather aggregation: aggregate hourly 'Date_time' rows to daily grain before feature construction; join on date; impute or truncate pre-2015 weather NaN rather than forward-fill from 2015 boundary
durable_rules.why: weather coverage starts 2015; 5 of 10 training years are weather-NaN; imputing across the 2010-2015 gap with 2015 values would inject false signal
durable_rules.cost_if_broken: imputed weather values would be uncorrelated with actual 2010-2014 weather; may appear to reduce MAE if the model over-indexes on a 2015 boundary artifact

durable_rules.rule: Competitor features: use VerlofConcurrent.csv ONLY (not VerlofConcurrent_2.csv); join on date; pre-2017 rows get 0/null
durable_rules.why: VC2 is an exact duplicate of VC1 with one extra identifier column; using both would duplicate the signal and could cause multicollinearity issues
durable_rules.cost_if_broken: duplicate feature inflates feature importance scores; may not measurably hurt MAE but produces misleading diagnostics

durable_rules.rule: Deliverydata (all three files) must not be used as features
durable_rules.why: wholesale delivery channel; no branch 01 retail sales tie-in; confirmed NOT_USED in this run and prior runs
durable_rules.cost_if_broken: delivery quantities are lagged and aggregated differently from retail demand; using them would introduce noise or data leakage (delivery anticipates demand)

methodological_cautions.caution: Zero-demand days (50 total) are a mixture of public holidays, COVID closures, and possibly system outages — they are NOT randomly distributed and must be treated differently
methodological_cautions.why: 2020 has 24 zero-demand days (COVID lockdown March-May 2020); prior years have 3-14 per year (likely Belgian public holidays and sporadic closures); building naive predictor features on same-DOW lookbacks will pick up these zeros as signal if not flagged
methodological_cautions.cost_if_ignored: naive features built on windows containing zero-demand days will under-predict on adjacent days; model may learn a spurious 'post-holiday dip' pattern

methodological_cautions.caution: 2014 has only 64 trading days (should be ~250); cause unknown but confirmed by protocol.json
methodological_cautions.why: rolling-origin CV folds that include 2014 as a 'full year' will have biased train set sizes; any annual seasonality feature computed on 2014 will be sparse
methodological_cautions.cost_if_ignored: annual seasonality features that look back to 2014 may pick up the sparse year as low-demand period; CV fold boundaries that straddle 2013-2015 will have uneven time coverage

methodological_cautions.caution: Post-regime level drop of -10.5% (pre-mean 318.3, post-mean 285.0) is confounded by COVID closures in early 2020
methodological_cautions.why: 2020-01-01 to 2020-05-31 has 24 zero-demand days (COVID); if those are excluded, the pre-regime non-zero mean for 2020 would be higher; the regime change also happens at the same time as post-lockdown recovery; the structural break is real but its magnitude is uncertain
methodological_cautions.cost_if_ignored: models that estimate a regime-level shift using raw means will over-estimate the magnitude of the drop; post-regime demand may recover toward pre-regime levels as COVID effect dissipates in 2021 (outside training set)

methodological_cautions.caution: Weather temporal column is 'Date_time'; do not assume standard column names
methodological_cautions.why: weather parquet file uses a non-standard column name; using 'date' or 'timestamp' will raise KeyError or silently produce NaT-filled series
methodological_cautions.cost_if_ignored: weather aggregation code fails silently or produces all-null weather features, removing weather signal without an error

methodological_cautions.caution: Bread articles catalog count (278) is NOT the count of articles sold in branch 01 (139 per prior runs); do not use catalog count as validation of data loading
methodological_cautions.why: productdata.csv contains the full chain catalog; 139 is the count of argcod=1 articles with at least one sale recorded in branch 01 XML files; using 278 as a check would never catch missing articles
methodological_cautions.cost_if_ignored: Preprocess may accept a data load that is missing up to half the bread article lines without triggering a count mismatch warning

methodological_cautions.caution: ACF at lag-1 is lower (0.325) than expected for daily retail; dominant seasonality is the weekly pattern (lag-6=0.582); short-lag features alone are insufficient
methodological_cautions.why: within-week DOW variance is the primary structure; day-to-day carry-forward is secondary; ARIMA(1,0,0) or pure AR(1) models will miss the dominant pattern
methodological_cautions.cost_if_ignored: AR-only time series models will under-perform relative to DOW-aware models; training skill must include at least one model with explicit DOW features or seasonal AR terms
